questions.question: box-sizing: border-box makes width include:
questions.explanation: With border-box, the declared width is the total box size; padding/border are subtracted internally. Margin stays outside.

questions.question: An element with width:100px, padding:10px, border:2px, box-sizing:content-box renders at total width:
questions.explanation: content-box adds padding+border to the width, so 100+20+4 = 124px total.

questions.question: Padding is the space:

options.text: Between the content and the border (inside the box)

questions.explanation: Padding is inner spacing (content→border). Margin is outer (border→neighbors).

questions.question: Margin is the space:

options.text: Outside the border, separating the element from others

questions.explanation: Margin is the outermost spacing; it is transparent and pushes siblings away. Not part of the element's background.

questions.question: A common reset is:

options.text: * { box-sizing: border-box; } so widths are predictable

questions.explanation: The universal border-box reset makes sizing intuitive across the app — a near-universal best practice.

questions.question: Background (color/image) fills:
questions.explanation: Background extends through padding to the border edge; margin is always transparent and outside the background.

questions.question: box-sizing: content-box is the:

options.text: Default (CSS spec) value — width applies to content only

questions.explanation: The initial value is content-box; that's why a reset to border-box is so common.

questions.question: Total element outer width equals:
questions.explanation: Outer footprint = the box (content+padding+border) plus margin on each side. Border-box width already includes the first three.
